import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Euclid Numbers conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid_number)
-/

namespace EuclidNumbers

/--
The n-th Euclid number is the product of the first n prime numbers plus one.
-/
noncomputable def Euclid (n : ℕ) : ℕ := 1 + ∏ i ∈ Finset.range n, i.nth Nat.Prime

/--
It is not known whether there is an infinite number of prime Euclid numbers.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem infinite_prime_euclid_numbers : answer(sorry) ↔ {n | (Euclid n).Prime}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
It is not known whether every Euclid number is a square-free number.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem euclid_numbers_are_square_free : answer(sorry) ↔ (∀ n, Squarefree (Euclid n)) := by
  sorry

end EuclidNumbers

reformulations.difference: Lean asks for infinitely many indices n : ℕ with prime Euclid n, whereas Wikipedia asks for infinitely many distinct prime Euclid numbers and starts its displayed sequence at n = 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For positive n, the definition is exactly the product of the first n primes plus one. Each prime is at least 2 and every partial product is positive, so Euclid is strictly increasing and hence injective. Infinitely many qualifying indices therefore give exactly infinitely many distinct qualifying values. Removing the single index 0 does not affect infinitude. The equivalence with infinitude of {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ ∃ n > 0, Euclid n = p} was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean quantifies over all natural indices, including 0, rather than just the positive indices used by Wikipedia.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The empty product gives Euclid 0 = 2, which is square-free. Thus squarefreeness at every natural index is equivalent to squarefreeness at every positive index. Mathlib's Squarefree on ℕ also agrees with the ordinary condition that no prime square divides the number. Both equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: All three declarations were checked. Nat.nth Nat.Prime is zero-indexed and never reaches its fallback value because the primes are infinite. Lean verified Euclid 0 through Euclid 6 as 2, 3, 7, 31, 211, 2311, 30031, including the first composite value 30031 = 59 × 509. The scratch file compiles, and its equivalence proofs have no sorry dependencies. Both research-open tags match Wikipedia's explicit current descriptions. Supplemental OEIS and AMS requests returned browser challenges; their contents were not used.
